speaker: Doctor
text: I need to start by understanding the timeline and nature of your symptoms. Have these night sweats and weight loss been occurring for more than two weeks, and have you experienced any recent fevers? Additionally, are you currently taking any new medications or supplements?

speaker: Patient
text: I have been feeling very tired and have had worsening abdominal pain for about four weeks. I have also had drenching night sweats and lost about twelve pounds.

speaker: Doctor
text: That is concerning, especially the combination of "B symptoms" (fevers, night sweats, weight loss) with lymphadenopathy and abdominal pain. Have you noticed any specific lumps in your neck or armpits, or any changes in your bowel habits like constipation or diarrhea? Also, do you have any history of HIV, recent travel, or new sexual partners?

speaker: Patient
text: I noticed swelling in my neck over the last few days. It does not hurt, but it feels enlarged and fixed.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Hodgkin Lymphoma. The combination of "B symptoms" (fever, night sweats, weight loss), painless supraclavicular lymphadenopathy that is fixed, and abdominal pain is highly suggestive of advanced-stage Hodgkin Lymphoma. I recommend a CT scan of the neck, chest, and abdomen to stage the disease and a lymph node biopsy for confirmation.
